releases.title: Public MVP
releases.goal: Hikma AI ships as a neutral open-source CLI: brew on macOS and Linux, an install script elsewhere, and skills from any repo.
releases.exit: A public repo with a tagged release installs via brew and the install script, installs and pushes skills against a real registry, and contains no bundled registry.

releases.title: Lifecycle and reach
releases.goal: Manage the full skill lifecycle and install at project or user scope for more agents.
releases.exit: Users can remove, diff, and restore skills from the lockfile, install globally, and use at least two more agents.

releases.title: Trust
releases.goal: Make installs verifiable and releases signed.
releases.exit: Frozen installs from the lockfile, skill verification, and signed release artifacts are available.

releases.title: Stable
releases.goal: Stable contracts, hardened quality, and complete docs.
releases.exit: Config keys, the lockfile format, and the skill layout are documented and versioned; CI covers all supported platforms end to end.

phases.title: Foundation and Rebrand
phases.goal: Create a Claude-only planning repo and define the safe migration path into Hikma AI.
phases.exit: The repo has agentkan planning, Claude instructions, and a reviewed migration checklist with no organization references.

epics.title: Claude-only project foundation
epics.goal: Set up the repo so Claude can operate from one board and one instruction file.
epics.exit: CLAUDE.md, docs/board, and the local agentkan Claude skill exist and validate.

tasks.title: Add Claude-only project instructions
Install the agentkan skill for Claude
Validate the board schema

epics.title: Public identity and naming
epics.goal: Lock the public identity around Hikma AI and the hikma CLI.
epics.exit: README, command examples, package names, and release text consistently use Hikma AI and hikma.

tasks.title: Confirm project name, CLI name, and repository slug
Write neutral positioning and tagline
Choose license and contribution posture

epics.title: Source import audit
epics.goal: Identify exactly what can be copied, renamed, generalized, rewritten, or omitted for the public CLI-only tool.
epics.exit: A migration checklist exists for code, templates, docs, workflows, package metadata, and the removal of bundled registry behavior.

tasks.title: Inventory commands, packages, templates, tests, and release files
List private defaults and organization-specific references to remove
Identify bundled registry files and behaviors to omit
Decide import strategy: history copy, clean copy, or rewrite

phases.title: CLI With External Registries
phases.goal: Make the CLI usable by any internet user with their own separate registry repository.
phases.exit: A user can initialize Hikma AI, point it at a separate registry such as hasankhatib/ai, and install or update skills without private assumptions or bundled registry content.

epics.title: User-owned registry configuration
epics.goal: Replace fixed registry assumptions with explicit user-owned registry configuration.
epics.exit: The CLI can read, set, validate, and use a registry URL from project or user config, including github.com/hasankhatib/ai.

tasks.title: Design config precedence for project, user, env, and flag values
Add commands to view and set the active registry
Support GitHub registry shorthand such as hasankhatib/ai
Validate registry shape before install or update operations
Add config list/get/set/unset/path, showing each value and its source (flag, env, project, user)
Support committed project config at .hikma/config.json in the precedence chain
Fold hikma tap into config list and doctor; keep config registry/agent as aliases
Pass the resolved registry explicitly instead of setting HIKMA_REGISTRY from --registry
Config hygiene: stop project lookup at $HOME, delete config file when unset empties it, set APPDATA in config tests
Add naming key (loose|kebab-case, default loose) via config set; enforce it only in create, push, and registry validate
Fold hikma config agent and config registry into config set (keep as hidden aliases) and add --json to list-style commands

epics.title: Neutral scaffold templates
epics.goal: Ship templates that work for general open-source and private projects.
epics.exit: Generated files mention only the user's project, selected agent, and configured registry.

tasks.title: Rewrite generated agent instructions for neutral usage
Support Claude-first scaffolding without opencode files
Add examples for public, private, and local registries
Ensure generated files do not assume this repo contains a registry
Make hikma init choose the agent (flag or prompt) and install skills into that agent folder (.claude/skills, .agents/skills)
Keep the CLI agent-neutral: agent layouts live in one table, independent of this repo being Claude-only
Project config gets an agents list and init installs into each listed agent folder; agent stays a per-user default
Verify each agent layout (skills dir, instruction file) against that tool docs before release

epics.title: Skill lifecycle for public users
epics.goal: Make skill list, install, create, update, and publish flows work with external registries.
epics.exit: Skill lifecycle commands are documented, tested, and independent of any fixed registry owner or in-repo skills folder.

tasks.title: Generalize skill discovery and install paths
Define registry contribution and publishing flow for external repos
Document expected external registry directory structure
Verify commands never read skills from the Hikma AI repo itself
Read public repos without gh via git clone --depth 1; require gh only for the GitHub API push flow and private repos
Accept GitHub owner/repo, any git URL, or a local path as a skill source
Add hikma registry validate (frontmatter, naming convention, layout) and finish the source-repo spec; discovery without an index is done
Record each install in .hikma/lock.json (source repo, commit SHA, file hashes); update uses the recorded source, blocks on local edits, and lists changed files (flags scripts/)
Add a source layer (git clone and local path checkouts, skill discovery) and route list, info, install, update through it; output via cmd.OutOrStdout()
Install syntax: hikma skill install <owner/repo> <name> [--ref], bare <name> uses the configured registry, and owner/repo alone opens a picker (non-TTY lists and exits)
Install path safety only: name must be a single path segment inside the skills directory; no naming convention enforced on install
Print the source repo and ref on every install and update
Push gate: always show the target registry and its config source and require confirmation (--yes skips for scripts)
Push via fork and PR when there is no write access and stop force-updating an existing skill branch (default branch lookup and opt-in CODEOWNERS are done)

epics.title: CLI-only repository boundary
epics.goal: Keep Hikma AI as only the CLI source repo, not a default or bundled skill registry.
epics.exit: The repo has no top-level skills registry and tests prove the registry must come from config, flags, or user selection.

tasks.title: Remove or omit top-level registry content from the public repo
Define safe sample registry references without making them defaults
Add tests that fail when a hidden bundled registry is used

phases.title: Open Source Release
phases.goal: Prepare the public repository for outside users and repeatable releases.
phases.exit: A tagged release is available with binaries, installation docs, and clear contribution guidance.

epics.title: Build, test, and quality gates
epics.goal: Establish confidence that the public CLI builds and behaves correctly.
epics.exit: CI runs formatting, tests, and a build for every pull request.

Add CI for test and build checks
Verify no private names, URLs, or credentials are present
Add tests for install, update, push gate and registry parsing using local fixture repos (after the Backend interface)

epics.title: Public documentation
epics.goal: Explain Hikma AI clearly to first-time users and registry owners.
epics.exit: README and docs cover install, init, registry setup with an external repo, skill install, skill creation, and troubleshooting.

tasks.title: Write README with quickstart and project model
Add command reference for the MVP
Add registry owner guide
Document using hasankhatib/ai as a personal registry example

Add issue templates, a changelog, and a review of SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md before going public

epics.title: Release packaging
epics.goal: Publish Hikma AI through normal open-source release channels.
epics.exit: Users can install a released hikma binary from GitHub releases and documented package channels.

epics.title: Documentation site and pages
epics.goal: Keep a public docs site option while allowing a Cloudflare Pages presence under alkhatib.tech.
epics.exit: The repo can publish GitHub Pages docs and the docs content can also be deployed or linked from alkhatib.tech.

phases.title: Lifecycle and Reach
phases.goal: Round out skill management and widen where and for whom skills install.
phases.exit: Remove, diff, sync, global installs, and more agents work and are documented.

epics.title: Complete skill lifecycle
epics.goal: Add the missing lifecycle commands around install and update.
epics.exit: Users can remove, list, diff, and restore skills from the lockfile.

tasks.title: hikma skill remove <name>: delete the installed folders and lock entries for the selected agents
hikma skill list --installed: show installed skills, source, commit, and whether files were edited
hikma skill diff <name>: show local edits and upstream changes
hikma sync: restore every skill in .hikma/lock.json on a fresh clone, like npm ci

epics.title: Global installs
epics.goal: Install skills at user scope as well as project scope.
epics.exit: --global installs into each agent's user skills folder with its own lockfile.

tasks.title: Add user-scope skills dirs to the agent layout table and verify each against the tool docs
Add --global to install, update, remove, and list with a lockfile under the user config dir
Document precedence when a skill exists at both scopes

epics.title: More agents
epics.goal: Support additional agents through the layout table.
epics.exit: At least two more agents install skills and instruction files to their documented locations.

tasks.title: Verify documented skill and instruction locations for Cursor and Gemini CLI
Add layout entries and templates for the verified agents

phases.title: Trust
phases.goal: Let users verify what they install and what they download.

epics.title: Verifiable installs
epics.exit: A frozen sync fails on any drift, and skill verify reports tampering.

tasks.title: hikma sync --frozen: fail if the lockfile and installed files differ or a commit cannot be fetched
hikma skill verify: re-hash installed files against the lockfile
Optional registry checksum manifest checked on install
Confirm before applying an update that changes scripts/

epics.goal: Sign release artifacts so downloads can be verified.
epics.exit: Release archives carry signatures or attestations and the install script verifies them.

phases.exit: Documented, versioned formats and platform-complete CI.
